analysis.title: Macro at a Glance: Latest views and forecasts
key_insights: GS revised its BoJ forecast and now expects an additional hike in March 2027. The reason given is that scaling down government energy subsidies should lift core CPI in early 2027.
Global real GDP is forecast to grow 2.8% yoy in 2027. Lower energy prices and strong AI investment growth offset tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy.
Global core inflation is forecast to slow to 2.4% by end-2027, mainly because the boost from energy price passthrough fades.

US real GDP is forecast to grow 2.4% Q4/Q4 in 2027, above consensus, helped by the AI capex boom and lower energy prices. Core PCE is forecast to fall to 2.4% yoy by end-2027 as the effects of tariffs, energy passthrough and AI price pressures diminish. Unemployment is forecast to end 2027 at 4.2%.
GS expects two more 25bp Fed hikes, in December 2026 and March 2027, to a peak range of 4.25-4.5%. Gradual cuts would start in November 2027 and end at a terminal range of 3.25-3.5%.

Euro area real GDP growth is forecast to slow to 0.9% Q4/Q4 in 2027, on delayed energy cost passthrough to consumers and tighter financial conditions, especially in France. Core inflation is forecast to peak at 2.9% yoy in 2Q27.
The ECB is expected to deliver one more 25bp hike in December to a 2.75% peak policy rate. It would then normalize toward a 2.25% terminal rate in 4Q27.

China real GDP growth is forecast at 4.5% yoy in 2027 on continued export strength and fading property and fiscal drags. CPI/PPI inflation is forecast to fall to 0.5%/0.3% next year, largely on lower commodity prices.

The two risks GS flags are the Middle East conflict, including risks to the region's energy exports, and AI capex disappointments. The capex risk could come from regulation, capacity constraints or credit market stress.
